name: Hoola
description: Hoola (or Hulla) is a popular Korean rummy game related to the Japanese game Seven Bridge. It is a fast-paced game of sets and runs, where the goal is to empty your hand. It features unique mechanics like 'Blasts' (winning with specific sevens) and 'Knocking' (claiming a win when your point total is low).

overview.description: Hoola (or Hulla) is a popular Korean rummy game related to the Japanese game Seven Bridge. It is a fast-paced game of sets and runs, where the goal is to empty your hand. It features unique mechanics like 'Blasts' (winning with specific sevens) and 'Knocking' (claiming a win when your point total is low).

history.origins: Likely developed in the late 20th century as an evolution of Western and Japanese Rummy variants (specifically Seven Bridge). It became a dominant social game in Korea.
timeline: 1980s: Hoola emerges in Korean gathering places.
1990s: Rules stabilize into the 'Battle Hoola' format.
Present: One of the most common casual card games in Korea, with many mobile versions.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a social 'filler' game or for small stakes (e.g., in PC bangs or among friends).
history.evolution: The game evolved from a standard 'draw and discard' rummy into a more aggressive version where players can 'battle' for the discard.

setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards to each player (anticlockwise). The remaining cards form the stock.

rules.objective: Win by melding all cards in your hand or having the lowest point total when someone 'knocks'.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players draw from the stock or claim the discard.
2. **Battle**: If multiple players want the discard, there is a priority system (usually the next player in order has first right).
3. **Melding**: - **Sets**: 3 or 4 cards of the same rank. - **Runs**: 3+ consecutive cards of the same suit (Cyclic: K-A-2 is allowed). - **Sevens**: A single 7 can be melded alone.
4. **Blast**: Winning with a specific combination involving 7s or a clean sweep of the hand recorded as a 'Blast' (double points).
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Hoola.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - Face cards: 10-13 pts.
Winning condition: Win by melding all cards in your hand or having the lowest point total when someone 'knocks'.

strategy.basic: Prioritize melding your high cards (Kings, Queens) first to reduce your point total in case someone else wins.
strategy.intermediate: Keep a 7 in your hand until you can use it to 'close' out a hand or as a safe exit. Melding a 7 alone is a good way to reduce your count.
strategy.advanced: The 'Battle' strategy: Don't just take the discard because you need it; take it to prevent an opponent from matching it if they are close to emptying their hand.
tips: Watch the discard pile; in Hoola, cards can turn the corner (K-A-2), making Aces very flexible.
If you have a 7, remember it's a 'double penalty' (14 pts) if it stays in your hand.

variations.name: Hoola without Battles
variations.description: Discard can only be taken when it is your turn; if multiple want it, the player whose turn is earlier gets it. Or play non-battle: only the player to your left's discard can be taken, on your turn.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine overrides needed for turn-order variant.

variations.name: Six or Seven Players
variations.description: With 6 or 7 players, one or two drop out after the deal so exactly five play. Dealer cannot drop out; forced drop-outs may claim compensation for sevens, sets or sequences.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Player count and drop-out rules; overrides to be added when supported.

variations.name: Hoola Multiplier
variations.description: Some play that the multiplier for going out with a Perfect (all 7 cards melded at once) is only double, not quadruple.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes multiplier constant; no engine overrides identified yet.

scoring.description: Players score points for cards in hand. Melding reduces point total. First to meld all cards or lowest total when knocked wins.
scoring.winCondition: Empty hand first, or lowest point total when someone knocks.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast-paced Korean rummy game where players meld sets and runs, with knock mechanics and aggressive discard battles.
